SE to run 1k-query throughput and p95 latency bench on Emberly sample dataset (Priya) - by 2025-09-17
Emberly to provide redacted sample dataset + typical prompt templates (Maya) - by 2025-09-12
Share SOC2/ISO docs and network diagram (Redwood) - by 2025-09-12
Schedule procurement intro (Carlos + Jordan) - week of 2025-09-15
action_items: Priya Shah - run perf bench: 1k queries, 256 token avg, measure p50/p95/p99 and token cost - due 2025-09-17
Carlos Mendez - send POC commercial guardrails (credits, term, sample SOW) - due 2025-09-12

meeting_header:
Date: 2025-09-10
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 57 minutes
Attendees: Carlos Mendez (Redwood AE), Priya Shah (Redwood SE), Liam O'Connor (Redwood CSM); Maya Torres (Head of Data, Emberly), Ravi Patel (Platform Eng), Susan Kim (CTO), Jordan White (Procurement)
summary: POC scoping call to define success criteria, workload sizing, benchmarks and timeline. Discussed commercial guardrails for a 4-week pilot: $25k credits, usage caps, reporting, and path to procurement if POC successful. SE to run benchmarks on Emberly sample data; Redwood to share SOC2/ISO docs and POC SOW. Procurement will need PO and SOW for pilot; potential path to Dedicated capacity if metrics met.
topics: POC timeline and pilot terms (credits, caps, duration)
transcript:
[00:00] Carlos: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, this is Carlos from Redwood, I run the AE for Emberly, with me is Priya our SE and Liam from CSM. Uh, quick roll call?
[00:10] Maya: Maya here.
[00:12] Ravi: Ravi on the line.
[00:14] Susan: Susan here.
[00:16] Jordan: Jordan here.
[00:20] Carlos: Awesome, thanks. The goal for today is to scope a POC — specifically success criteria, what workloads you want us to run, and the commercial guardrails like credits and terms. Priya will talk tech, I'll cover commercial.
[01:05] Priya: Cool, quick context question, Maya — can you remind us what your current inference stack looks like? Are you running a mix of on-prem and cloud, and do you have any latency targets today?
[01:20] Maya: Yeah so currently we host models in AWS EKS, mostly in EC2 GPU instances for batch scoring. Near real-time features go through a small CPU-based endpoint which is a bottleneck. Latency target for product is p95 < 250ms end-to-end; from model side we aim for p95 < 150ms. Throughput varies: peak about 120 req/s for inference across peaks, average closer to 30-40.
[02:00] Ravi: To add, we have a couple of multi-turn flows so average token length is around 200-300 tokens per request.
[02:15] Priya: Great — that helps. For the POC we'd suggest running two benchmark modes: a latency-focused test (single-stream, cold cache and warm) to measure p50/p95/p99, and a throughput test with batching to see sustainable req/s and token cost.
[02:40] Carlos: On the commercial side we typically offer POC credits and a short pilot SOW. For this scale, we usually propose $20-30k in credits for a 3-4 week pilot, with a soft usage cap so we don't blow past expectations. The pilot would include basic support and a single model variant on hosted or dedicated (you can choose), and then if successful we move to contracting.
[03:10] Susan: When you say hosted vs dedicated — what are the tradeoffs? We care about predictability and data isolation.
[03:20] Priya: Hosted is fastest to start — no infra setup, but shared pools; you get predictable performance for most workloads but can see variability in noisy-neighbor cases. Dedicated gives reserved GPU pools, predictable throughput and more isolation — and for Emberly's compliance needs we can run Private or Dedicated with encryption to customer KMS. There's a delta in cost; dedicated is higher but more predictable.
[03:55] Maya: For the POC we prefer hosted to move fast, but isolation and SOC2 logs are important for audit. Do you provide audit logs in hosted?
[04:05] Liam: Yes — hosted by Redwood includes request/response level audit logs for the POC retention window; for longer-term retention or specific SOC2 requirements we can push to Private or add logging retention as an add-on. We'll share our SOC2 and ISO documentation.
[04:35] Ravi: On encryption, do you support customer-managed keys?
[04:38] Priya: Yep, for Dedicated and Private we integrate with KMS/HSM; hosted can be configured with VPC peering and encryption at rest in our managed offering. We'll share the exact network diagram.
[05:05] Carlos: Back to guardrails — the POC commercial terms we'd propose: 4 week pilot, $25k in credits, a soft usage cap of e.g. 100k generated tokens/day to prevent runaway tests, standard POC SOW, and a simple acceptance criteria doc that you sign off on. If you hit acceptance we provide a path to production with either a monthly reserved capacity quote or private deployment SOW.
[05:45] Jordan: On procurement side, what paperwork do we need to spin up this pilot? We typically need an SOW and a PO.
[05:55] Carlos: Right — we can provide a short SOW that describes scope, duration, credits and liability terms. Procurement would need that plus a PO; contracts team can run a standard pilot MSA.
[06:15] Jordan: Ok that sounds reasonable. Any minimum liability or add'l clauses?
[06:20] Carlos: For pilots we keep it simple: standard limitation of liability to pilot value, IP stays with customer for prompts/data. We'll send a redlined sample.
[06:35] Priya: Back to benchmarks — we should nail success criteria now: Maya, does the team have specific quantitative goals? For example: p95 latency <= 200ms for 256 token average, throughput >= 100 req/s with batching at p95 < 300ms, and regression on quality <= 3-5% measured by your eval set?
[07:00] Maya: Yes those are good starting points. We'll prepare an eval set where we can measure F1 and hallucination rate. For product sign-off we want no more than a 5% drop in existing metrics.
[07:15] Ravi: Also capture memory/KV cache behavior for multi-turn flows. We have long sessions so cache hit rate impacts latency.
[07:25] Priya: We'll instrument KV cache metrics, token throughput and per-request latency, and include cold-start/warm cache runs.
[07:40] [audio hiccup]
[08:00] Susan: One question on benchmarking: will Redwood run the tests in your hosted infra or do you want us to mirror in our environment?
[08:10] Priya: We generally run both: Redwood runs a baseline in hosted to measure what you'd see on our side, and we can run a mirror test in your environment for network/diff noise. For an apples-to-apples cost estimate we run token cost modeling on the benchmark outputs.
[08:30] Carlos: Commercial note: credits cover compute and model use for the pilot; data transfer and add-on observability have to be scoped. We'll call out any additional charges in the SOW.
[08:50] Maya: For the model, are we bringing our own model or using Redwood-curated open models? We have a fine-tuned model we'd like to test on Emberly prompts.
[09:00] Priya: You can bring your own model — we'll support private model deployment in Dedicated/Private, or we can run it in hosted under a tenant if it's ok. We might need model files and containerization details. For performance, quantization profiles matter; we'll recommend them after initial bench.
[09:20] Ravi: Is there a recommended tokenization or prompt format to minimize cost?
[09:25] Priya: Usually instruct-style prompts with short system prefixes and structured inputs help. Also we can suggest batching, prefix caching and KV cache ways to cut per-token cost. We'll include batching configs in the bench plan.
[09:45] Carlos: On timeline — we aim to kick off within a week of agreement. Week 0: SOW signed and data shared; Week 1: Redwood runs baseline hosted benchmarks; Week 2: run customer-mirroring and accuracy evals; Week 3: results, fine-tuning adjustments; Week 4: final report and acceptance.
[10:10] Maya: That timeline is fine. Procurement needs to know estimated cost to convert after POC — can we get a ballpark for Dedicated reserved capacity?
[10:20] Carlos: We'll include rough monthly committed pricing in the POC quote but final depends on target throughput and GPU type. For your scale (100 req/s and 200-300 token avg) we'd likely recommend a 4-GPU reserved pool or a managed private cluster. Ballpark monthly committed pricing we'll include in the proposal.
[10:45] Jordan: If the POC goes well, what is the expected procurement cycle? We typically need 4-6 weeks depending on legal review.
[10:55] Carlos: That's typical. Good to start legal early — we can coordinate an initial procurement/contract intro next week.
[11:10] Priya: Technical note: we'll need sample traces with timestamps and a few representative long sessions; also if you have a golden set of expected outputs that helps measure hallucination and regression.
[11:25] Maya: We'll prepare a 5k redacted dataset and a 200-case golden evaluation set.
[11:35] Priya: Great. For the benchmark we'll run three passes: cold cache single-stream latency, warm cache single-stream latency, and throughput with batching at varying batch sizes to find sweet spot. We'll share config and scripts in a repo.
[12:00] Ravi: How do you measure token cost? Is it per generated token or input+output?
[12:06] Carlos: We bill per token (input + output combined) for hosted API. For pilot credits we'll reconcile using our normal metering. We'll include sample cost scenarios in the quote.
[12:20] [background chatter]
[12:45] Maya: A couple of security questions: do you support SSO/SAML for console access, and role-based access controls?
[12:52] Liam: Yes both — SSO (SAML/OIDC) and RBAC are supported for team onboarding. We'll include instructions for setting up just-in-time access for the pilot.
[13:10] Susan: For audit and compliance we need log retention for 90 days, is that standard?
[13:18] Liam: Default is 30 days for the hosted pilot, but we can extend retention as an add-on or via Private deployment. We'll note options in the SOW.
[13:35] Priya: Another note: if you plan to test a fine-tuned model, tokenization and compiled kernels will affect performance. We'll capture quantization suggestions (int8/int4) post-benchmark; but initial runs on FP16 or bfloat are simplest.
[14:00] Carlos: Anything else on the commercial guardrails? We're proposing $25k credits, 4-week pilot, soft cap 100k tokens/day, SOW + PO to start. Acceptance criteria: meet latency and accuracy thresholds discussed and sign-off from Maya and Susan.
[14:25] Jordan: That seems ok. Need to confirm whether POC value is recognized on our side for internal budget; we prefer a no-cash pilot with credits and a PO to cover administrative needs.
[14:40] Carlos: That's standard. We'll provide a short SOW and an invoiceable PO for the pilot value.
[14:55] Maya: On the evaluation metrics: we'll flag cases where model output is unsafe or needs guardrails — can Redwood help with red-team prompts?
[15:05] Priya: We have prompt-safety tooling and can run a small red-team evaluation during the POC. We'll include that in the bench plan.
[15:25] [sound of keyboard]
[15:40] Carlos: Okay to recap next steps: Redwood to share SOW, POC guardrails and SOC2 docs by Friday; SE runs baseline bench once we have sample data; Emberly to share dataset and prompts; procurement intro scheduled for week of 9/15.
[16:05] Maya: Sounds good.
[16:08] Ravi: Agree.
[16:10] Susan: Thanks.
[16:12] Jordan: Thanks everyone.
[16:30] Carlos: We also discussed potential blockers: model hosting constraints, data residency for EU customers, and procurement lead time. We'll address each in the SOW notes.
[20:00] Priya: Quick technical aside — for multi-turn KV cache stress we may recommend our compiled kernels and grouping of sequences. This typically reduces p95 by 20-30% in our tests.
[25:00] Maya: If you can show sample numbers that would help our execs.
[25:15] Priya: We'll include a dashboard snapshot and estimated token cost scenarios for your throughput.
[30:00] Carlos: Any final questions?
[30:10] Maya: Not at the moment.
[30:15] Ravi: None.
[30:20] Susan: No.
[30:25] Jordan: No.
[30:30] Carlos: Great — we'll follow up with the docs. Thanks everyone.
[30:40] [meeting ends abruptly at 00:30:50 in recording due to local network cutoff, full call actually ~57 minutes; additional follow-up chat continued after this timestamp but not recorded cleanly]
